lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: side ratios determined by similarity, not by size
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: side ratios determined by similarity, not by size

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

items.prompt: A 3-4-5 triangle, θ opposite the side 3. Find sin θ.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: A right triangle has hypotenuse 13 and one leg 5. Find the other leg.
Express sin 55° as a cosine of another angle, and explain why the two are equal.
choices: cos 35°, because the two angles are complementary and swap the roles of opposite and adjacent
cos 125°, because the angles are supplementary
cos 145°, because the angles differ by a right angle
cos 55°, because sine and cosine are always equal

items.prompt: From a point 30 m from the base of a tower, the angle of elevation to the top is θ, and the tower is 16 m tall. Which equation correctly determines θ?
A right triangle has legs 3 and 4 and hypotenuse 5. Angle θ is opposite the leg of length 3. Find sin θ as an exact fraction in lowest terms.
A right triangle has hypotenuse 29 and one leg 20. Find the other leg.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: Express sin 56° as a cosine of another angle, and explain why the two are equal.
choices: cos 34°, because the two angles are complementary and swap the roles of opposite and adjacent
cos 124°, because the angles are supplementary
cos 56°, because sine and cosine are always equal
cos 146°, because the angles differ by a right angle

items.prompt: From a point 4 m from the base of a tower, the angle of elevation to the top is θ, and the tower is 3 m tall. Which equation correctly determines θ?
